plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Extreme / Symbol / Motorola WiNG WLAN devices. It reports per-device CPU utilization (1-minute load scaled by 10), memory usage derived from free/total KiB, and interface traffic (enterprise PEN 388, wingMIB 1.3.6.1.4.1.388.50).
name: Wireless

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: 1-minute CPU utilization of a WiNG-managed device in percent, from wingStatsDevSysInfoLoadLimitS0 (1.3.6.1.4.1.388.50.1.4.2.2.1.1.8). The SNMP value is 10 times the percentage; Starlark divides by 10 before storage. Values outside 0-100 after scaling are dropped.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: Memory utilization of a WiNG-managed device in percent, computed as (total-free)/total from wingStatsDevSysInfoTotalMem and wingStatsDevSysInfoFreeMem (1.3.6.1.4.1.388.50.1.4.2.2.1.1.2 / .1, kilobytes). Emitted only when total > 0 and 0 <= free <= total.

metrics.name: device_memory_total
metrics.description: Total memory of a WiNG-managed device in bytes, from wingStatsDevSysInfoTotalMem (1.3.6.1.4.1.388.50.1.4.2.2.1.1.2). The SNMP value is in kilobytes; Starlark multiplies by 1024 before storage.

metrics.name: device_memory_free
metrics.description: Free memory of a WiNG-managed device in bytes, from wingStatsDevSysInfoFreeMem (1.3.6.1.4.1.388.50.1.4.2.2.1.1.1). The SNMP value is in kilobytes; Starlark multiplies by 1024 before storage.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCInOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCOutOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the WiNG device since the last restart, derived from sysUpTime. Monitoring uptime helps administrators understand device stability and identify unexpected reboots.
